residue.text: Protected failure signature: N1 already has successful sender recognition but remains dashboard-pending at boundaries 0 through 3, clearing at boundary 4. This discrepancy survives the attack as a diagnostic timing sensor; pending alone does not establish unmet recognition.

The exceptional delay origin is unknown. Later sender adaptation and extra status-query demand are unobserved hypotheses; no new demand occurs in this window. Synthetic timings establish neither empirical network behavior nor a globally best schedule.

summary.text: Failed account: every registered pending identity needs recognition, so routine bulk necessarily advances P2. N1 contradicts that account: another receipt consumes service without adding recognition. Surviving function: registration enables requests independently of delivery; bulk economically groups genuinely unrecognized registered identities.

Conditional model proposal: when recognition and pending ledgers disagree for N1, use individuals during its stale-display window and defer bulk. Validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Request individuals N2,N3,N4 at ticks 0,1,2. At boundary 4 require N1 and previously recognized notices cleared, plus an empty queue; then bulk N5,N6. Request individuals N7 at tick 5 and N8 at tick 6. Predicted first deliveries are N2,N3,N4 at ticks 1,2,3 and N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 5,6,7,8. Eight registrations finish by boundary 6; eight recognitions by boundary 9 include initial N1. Six requests. This trace is predicted, not observed.

Closest rival: immediate routine bulk. Feasible probe: compare N1 registration, first-success recognition, and pending ledgers at boundary 0; observe clearing at boundary 4. Recognition despite pending diagnoses stale display and selects deferred bulk; absent recognition would indicate genuine unmet receipt demand. Immediate bulk predicts duplicate N1 service at tick 1; guarded scheduling predicts none. Defeat: contradictory ledgers or failed boundary-4 guard, more than six actions, or fewer than eight distinct recognitions.

Burden: six clerk validations, six dispatcher requests, and boundary ledger comparisons. Readable ledgers add no clerk labor. Audit registrations, distinct recognitions, actions, duplicates, failed deliveries and display timing separately. Added capacity, dashboard reconfiguration and endpoint repair are unavailable.
